engagement.client-report: Inventory API (HTTP port 8088, /health) intermittently unreachable on 2026-11-14; external monitor saw it down 07:04:03-07:04:48 UTC and 07:10:03-07:10:48 UTC; it recovered by itself. Ubuntu VM.
engagement.analyst: L3 Linux support (offline bundle review, bundle rca-damon-20261114-085441)

rca-phase2-analysis.executive-summary: The server itself stayed up; only the Inventory API process died. Each outage started at the exact second the Linux kernel killed the API because it hit its configured memory ceiling (320 MiB), and ended when systemd restarted it about 45 seconds later, which is why it "came back by itself". The memory growth is driven by the scheduled job that calls the API's /report endpoint every 2 minutes: each call appears to leave roughly 110 MB allocated, so the third call after every restart pushed the service over its limit. The problem became visible at 06:58 UTC, when the service was reconfigured and restarted without access to swap; before that the same growth was silently pushed to swap (684 MB). A third, unreported outage occurred at 07:16 UTC, and at collection time (08:55 UTC) the API had been stopped manually and was not listening on port 8088.

root-cause.summary: inventory-api.service was killed by the cgroup OOM killer at both reported outage times (confirmed) because its memory grows by about 110 MB per /report request and, after a 06:58 reconfiguration removed swap from the unit (MemoryMax 320 MiB, swap limit 0), the third /report call after each start exceeded the limit (mechanism probable: inferred from timing and systemd accounting, app source and unit file not in the bundle).

mechanism.step: 06:41:47 inventory-api.service is started for the first time in the log window; from 06:42:01 a root cron job calls curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/report every 2 minutes.

06:41-06:58: each /report call leaves memory allocated; the unit hits its 320 MiB memory limit and the excess is pushed to swap (systemd: 320M memory peak, 684.3M swap peak after 9 calls, about 110 MB per call; sar shows pswpout 62-225/s in the same windows).

06:58:23 a daemon-reload plus restart of the unit is performed from an interactive session; from then on the kernel reports the cgroup with memory limit 327680 kB and swap limit 0 kB, so the overflow can no longer go to swap.

The 1st and 2nd /report calls after a start fit under 320 MiB; the 3rd call (07:04:01, 07:10:01, 07:16:01) triggers an anonymous page fault in a worker thread that cannot be charged, and the memcg OOM killer kills python3 (anon-rss about 327 MB) within 0.1 s of the cron call.

systemd marks the unit failed (result oom-kill) and restarts it after about 45 s (Restart= with a ~45 s RestartSec, inferred); the API is unreachable for exactly that gap, matching the monitor windows 07:04:03-07:04:48 and 07:10:03-07:10:48.

root-cause.trigger: Root cron job curl -s -m 60 http://127.0.0.1:8088/report every 2 minutes (even minutes); the 3rd call after each (re)start pushes the cgroup over its 320 MiB limit.
root-cause.why-intermittent: The process restarts with a clean heap after each kill, so it takes 3 /report calls (about 6 minutes) to refill to the limit; this produces a regular 6-minute kill / 45-second outage cycle, which looks intermittent from the outside.
root-cause.why-now: The service and the /report cron job first appear on 2026-11-14 at 06:41-06:42 (no trace in syslog.1). Until 06:58:23 swap hid the growth; the reconfiguration and restart at 06:58:23 removed the swap allowance (swap limit 0 kB in every OOM report afterwards), turning slow swapping into hard OOM kills.
root-cause.contributing-factor: Hard memory cap with no swap and no MemoryHigh soft limit: the first sign of pressure is a SIGKILL rather than throttling or an alert.
Restart delay of about 45 s defines the outage length; a shorter RestartSec would shrink each outage to a few seconds (but would not fix the leak).
No change record: unit changes at 06:41:47 and 06:58:23 were done via systemctl daemon-reload in interactive sessions without a load test of /report under the new limit.
root-cause.confirm-by: (1) systemctl cat inventory-api.service (and drop-ins) to confirm MemoryMax=320M, MemorySwapMax=0, Restart/RestartSec=45s and what changed at 06:58:23; (2) on a test instance, call /report 3 times and watch systemctl show -p MemoryCurrent inventory-api grow by about 110 MB per call; (3) app team review of the /report handler (tracemalloc) for objects/buffers retained after the response.

finding.title: Memory retained per /report request (about 110 MB per call); 3rd call after each start hits the limit
finding.description: A root cron job calls /report every 2 minutes from 06:42:01. Every OOM kill happens about 0.1 s after the 3rd /report call since the last (re)start, and never after the 1st or 2nd. The killing allocation is an anonymous page fault in a short-lived worker thread (comm "Thread-NN (proc...", RIP in a memset-style rep stosb), consistent with a large buffer being allocated per request. Before swap was removed the unit reached 320M RAM + 684.3M swap after 9 calls (about 1004 MB / 9, about 110 MB per call). Mechanism inferred from timing and accounting; app source not available.

hypothesis.name: Host reboot, kernel crash or hang
hypothesis.reason: Only one boot (since 2026-10-28 08:41:47) covers the incidents; no panic, Oops, hung task or soft lockup; the journal is continuous through every outage.

hypothesis.name: Host-wide memory exhaustion / global OOM
hypothesis.reason: All kills are CONSTRAINT_MEMCG limited to inventory-api.service; host %memused at most 7.86% and over 6.5 GB available around the incidents.

hypothesis.name: Disk I/O stall from the 5-minute dd cron job
hypothesis.reason: dd uses oflag=direct (no page cache, not charged to the service cgroup), runs at :00/:05 minutes; the 07:04 and 07:16 kills happened with no dd running; await at most 3.08 ms, no I/O errors.

hypothesis.name: CPU saturation or hypervisor steal
hypothesis.reason: Load and steal negligible; the API used under 1 s of CPU per run.

hypothesis.name: Network / listen-queue problem on port 8088
hypothesis.reason: No NIC errors, no conntrack pressure; the only SYN-flood message is from 2026-10-28 on 127.0.0.1:9100; the outage gaps coincide exactly with the process being dead, not with network events.
hypothesis.evidence: TCP: request_sock_TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 127.0.0.1:9100. Sending cookies.

hypothesis.name: labtimer-demo.service failures
hypothesis.reason: Separate unit failing 2.5 h before the incidents with a permission error on its own log file; no interaction with inventory-api.

phase1-review.check: The 3 OOM kills on 2026-11-14 (07:04:01, 07:10:01, 07:16:01) are the inventory-api outages (CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, inventory-api.service). The other OOM lines counted are lab oomdemo units in user.slice on 2026-10-28, outside the window and unrelated.

inventory-api failures/restarts (3) are the outage itself, caused by STAB-03. The 2 labtimer-demo.service failures (04:21:30, 04:28:16) are a separate permission problem on /var/tmp/labtimer.log, unrelated to the outage but worth fixing.
ext4 errors are deliberate test injections on a loop device ("trigger_test_error ... comm tee: lab test" / "round2") on 2026-11-13 00:29-00:30; root filesystem not affected, no read-only mounts now.
The pswpout peak 224.91/s (06:50-07:00) is inventory-api spilling its per-request growth into swap before the 06:58:23 change removed swap; same leak, earlier stage. Not a host-wide swap storm.

ListenOverflows/ListenDrops=1781 are cumulative since 2026-10-28; the only related kernel message is a SYN flood on 127.0.0.1:9100 on 2026-10-28. During the outages the 8088 listener did not exist at all (process dead), which gives connection refused, not overflows.
A ~10-minute sar interval cannot resolve 45-second outages; move to 1-minute sampling (R-6).

recommendation.action: Confirm whether the Inventory API is supposed to be down right now (stopped manually at 07:17:59, port 8088 not listening at 08:55) and capture the current unit definition before anything else changes.
recommendation.command: systemctl status inventory-api.service --no-pager; systemctl cat inventory-api.service; systemctl show inventory-api.service -p MemoryMax,MemoryHigh,MemorySwapMax,Restart,RestartUSec,User; ls -la /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service.d/ /etc/cron.d/; ss -ltnp 'sport = :8088'

recommendation.action: If the API must run before the code fix: keep the 2-minute /report cron job disabled (it is the trigger) and start the service. If /report must run, call it no more than twice between planned restarts, or temporarily allow swap again via a drop-in (MemorySwapMax=512M) knowing it only delays the kill.
recommendation.risk: Low. If /report is still called by another client, the OOM cycle returns after 3 calls (about 6 min at the old rate).

recommendation.action: App team: reproduce and fix memory retention in the /report handler (buffer or result cache that is never released, or per-request threads keeping references). Verify with tracemalloc / memory_profiler on a test instance.
recommendation.command: On a test host: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -m 60 http://127.0.0.1:8088/report >/dev/null; systemctl show -p MemoryCurrent inventory-api.service; done
recommendation.risk: Test environment only; on production this reproduction would cause an OOM kill on the 3rd call.
recommendation.downtime: none on production; deploy of the fix needs one service restart (seconds)

recommendation.action: Harden the unit after the fix: keep MemoryMax as a guardrail, add MemoryHigh below it so pressure throttles and is visible before a kill, and shorten RestartSec so any future kill costs seconds, not 45 s. Size MemoryMax from a measured peak under real /report load.
recommendation.command:
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service.d && printf '[Service]
MemoryHigh=280M
RestartSec=5s
' > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service.d/50-rca-hardening.conf && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart inventory-api.service
recommendation.risk: Low. MemoryHigh throttles (slows) the service near the limit; a restart is needed to apply.
recommendation.rollback: rm /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service.d/50-rca-hardening.conf && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart inventory-api.service

recommendation.action: Put unit file and cron changes under change control (the 06:41, 06:58 and 07:17 changes have no record); load-test memory limits before tightening them (removing swap converted slow degradation into hard outages).
Sample sysstat every minute; alert on systemd "Failed with result 'oom-kill'" and on memory.events oom_kill for the unit; review why the external monitor did not record the 07:16 outage.
recommendation.command:
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/sysstat-collect.timer.d && printf '[Timer]
OnCalendar=
OnCalendar=*:*:00
' > /etc/systemd/system/sysstat-collect.timer.d/1min.conf && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart sysstat-collect.timer
recommendation.risk: Negligible (sa file grows about 10x, still small).
recommendation.rollback: rm /etc/systemd/system/sysstat-collect.timer.d/1min.conf && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart sysstat-collect.timer

validation.criterion: With the /report job re-enabled at its normal rate, MemoryCurrent of inventory-api.service stays flat (no ~110 MB step per call) over 24 h.
No "Failed with result 'oom-kill'" for inventory-api.service and NRestarts unchanged for 24 h; memory.events oom_kill stays 0.
External monitor shows no /health failures for 7 days; Phase 1 STAB-03 and STAB-06 return to pass on re-collection.
